title: Went all in for 3 weeks.
author: chopjohnGames
selftext:
I've worked in the game industry for over 15 years as a lead designer. I decided about four weeks to go out on my own and just try this vibe coding thing. I'm at a point in my life where I can, and I'm basically just chasing passions right now.  
  
The timing was perfect because around that time was the date of a pretty cool game jam that had a $35,000 prize pool. I originally intended for this to be a one-week project, but I ended up really getting into the development of this game (passion project!) and so decided to push it a little bit further.   
  
I thought this was an interesting illustration of what it looks like for someone of my experience to dedicate myself for 3 weeks creating what I would consider a game I'd want to play. There's a lot that I wasn't able to get done. I immediately got caught up in scope creep, and so that was a good lesson learned for the next time. But I'm definitely proud of the progress and wanted to share. This has been an incredible journey for me, both as a creator and as someone who wants to become more of an AI expert. Happy to answer any questions about workflow.

comments.author: chopjohnGames
comments.body:
In Monsters of Myth, you get to choose a God and go on true mythical adventures. The first one, called "The War of the Titans", has Zeus square off with his father, the Titan Cronus. There's also an arena where eight players compete against other players' builds. At its core, you can think of Monsters of Myth as an auto-battler deck-building game (sort of a cross between Teamfight Tactics and Slay the Spire).

Edited to add link: [https://w.run/chopjohn/monsters-of-myth](https://w.run/chopjohn/monsters-of-myth)

comments.author: Tasty-Midnight-25
comments.body: Very cool! Are you going to make this available on Steam?

replies.author: chopjohnGames
replies.body: Ideally, yes. But definitely down the road.

comments.author: Dappthekid
comments.body:
This looks pretty sweet! What model did you end up using? I'm currently using Claude for everything, besides GPT for some references. I do have about 10 years, on and off, of unreal engine experience, but wanted to see how well Claude could improve the time It takes. I've gotten Claude to do some cool things for my game, but I feel like there's way more it can do, and I just have to figure out how to push it further. 

Game looks good!

replies.author: chopjohnGames
replies.body: Thank you. I used Opus 5.5 Extra for most of the work. I'm really excited about some of the learnings I had in the past few weeks, and I'm actually excited to get started on my next game, which is either going to use Unity or Roblox. I haven't quite decided yet. :) I totally agree with you that we're just sort of touching the tip of the iceberg right now. The next year is going to be crazy!

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body: I'd personally go for Unity, and possibly down the road a slimmed-down version on Roblox.

comments.author: ApprehensiveYou8920
comments.body:
Nice concept, but the characters definitely need a bit of polish and spatial standardization.

Are the characters all SVG art? They do look clean, but I'm concerned that this might not be the best route for animation.

replies.author: chopjohnGames
replies.body: Indeed, they are all SVG art. I wrote a quick algorithm to try to get SVG art that looks better, and for the most part, it worked well, but the animation is just impossible. Due to the short time frame of the game jam, I decided just to go with it, but I totally agree that future games are going to likely go in a totally different direction because of the animation limitations.

replies.author: ApprehensiveYou8920
replies.body:
I'm curious what the workflow was. Did you do it all in Claude?

I hadn't even thought about turning my 2D characters into SVG, but that makes a lot of sense to get cleaner, more consistent character designs. It also stands out from other AI artwork and probably makes it easier to clean up all the extra detail that OpenAI throws in.  
  
It might make sense to start with OpenAI character sheets and convert them to SVG from there.

replies.author: chopjohnGames
replies.body: Well, I technically did it all in Claude, but I used ElevenLabs as an integration within Claude. I'd make the character sheets in ElevenLabs, which utilizes nano banana in most cases. Then I'd have the AI take the character sheets, trace the one I like, and convert it into an SVG. There was a lot of fine-tuning to get it to work correctly, but I think it does a pretty good job at this point. I tried to do all sorts of things to get it to animate better, but I felt like I was kicking tires, so I went with good enough.

comments.author: chopjohnGames
comments.body: Good to know. I was using medium at first and then went to extra for, I can't even remember why. Now I'm still using extra and probably burning unnecessary tokens, lol.

comments.author: chopjohnGames
comments.body: Thanks for the feedback. I think I agree with you.

comments.author: chopjohnGames
comments.body: Wait, what? You don't care about my studio name intro. Bro!!!!  No, I'm just kidding, and I totally agree with you. I was so pumped about the studio name intro, and I think that was definitely more for me, lol.

replies.author: FowardJames
replies.body: Haha my bad for coming across overly dramatic 🤣 I was rushing out the house when I saw this. Basically just cut to the gameplay, give people the good stuff

replies.author: chopjohnGames
replies.body: No worries at all. I actually think it's good advice. There's a time and a place to show your intros, and a teaser trailer on Reddit is not one of them.
